## [Technical Requirements](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html\#technical-requirements "Permalink to this headline")

Before creating your first Symfony application you must:

- Install PHP 8.4 or higher and these PHP extensions (which are installed and
enabled by default in most PHP 8 installations): [Ctype](https://www.php.net/book.ctype), [iconv](https://www.php.net/book.iconv),
[PCRE](https://www.php.net/book.pcre), [Session](https://www.php.net/book.session), [SimpleXML](https://www.php.net/book.simplexml), and [Tokenizer](https://www.php.net/book.tokenizer);
- [Install Composer](https://getcomposer.org/download/), which is used to install PHP packages.

Also, [install the Symfony CLI](https://symfony.com/download). This is optional, but it gives you a
helpful binary called `symfony` that provides all tools you need to
develop and run your Symfony application locally.

The `symfony` binary also provides a tool to check if your computer meets all
requirements. Open your console terminal and run this command:

```
1
```

```
$ symfony check:requirements
```

Note

The Symfony CLI is open source, and you can contribute to it in the
[symfony-cli/symfony-cli GitHub repository](https://github.com/symfony-cli/symfony-cli).

## [Creating Symfony Applications](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html\#creating-symfony-applications "Permalink to this headline")

Open your console terminal and run any of these commands to create a new Symfony
application:

```
1
2
3
4
5
```

```
# run this if you are building a traditional web application
$ symfony new my_project_directory --version="8.1.*" --webapp

# run this if you are building a microservice, console application or API
$ symfony new my_project_directory --version="8.1.*"
```

The only difference between these two commands is the number of packages
installed by default. The `--webapp` option installs extra packages to give
you everything you need to build a web application.

If you're not using the Symfony binary, run these commands to create the new
Symfony application using Composer:

```
1
2
3
4
5
6
7
```

```
# run this if you are building a traditional web application
$ composer create-project symfony/skeleton:"8.1.*" my_project_directory
$ cd my_project_directory
$ composer require webapp

# run this if you are building a microservice, console application or API
$ composer create-project symfony/skeleton:"8.1.*" my_project_directory
```

No matter which command you run to create the Symfony application, all of them
will create a new `my_project_directory/` directory, download some dependencies
into it and even generate the basic directories and files you'll need to get
started. In other words, your new application is ready!

Note

The project's cache and logs directory (by default, `<project>/var/cache/`
and `<project>/var/log/`) must be writable by the web server. If you have
any issue, read how to [set up permissions for Symfony applications](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup/file_permissions.html).

## [Setting up an Existing Symfony Project](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html\#setting-up-an-existing-symfony-project "Permalink to this headline")

In addition to creating new Symfony projects, you will also work on projects
already created by other developers. In that case, you only need to get the
project code and install the dependencies with Composer. Assuming your team uses
Git, set up your project with the following commands:

```
1
2
3
4
5
6
7
```

```
# clone the project to download its contents
$ cd projects/
$ git clone ...

# make Composer install the project's dependencies into vendor/
$ cd my-project/
$ composer install
```

You'll probably also need to customize your [.env file](https://symfony.com/doc/current/configuration.html#config-dot-env)
and do a few other project-specific tasks (e.g. creating a database). When
working on an existing Symfony application for the first time, it may be useful
to run this command which displays information about the project:

```
1
```

```
$ php bin/console about
```

## [Running Symfony Applications](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html\#running-symfony-applications "Permalink to this headline")

In production, you should install a web server like Nginx or Apache and
[configure it to run Symfony](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup/web_server_configuration.html). This
method can also be used if you're not using the Symfony local web server for
development.

However for local development, the most convenient way of running Symfony is by
using the [local web server](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup/symfony_cli.html#symfony-cli-server) provided by the
Symfony CLI tool. This local server provides support for HTTP/2, concurrent
requests, TLS/SSL and automatic generation of security certificates, among
other things.

Open your terminal, move into your new project directory and start the local web
server as follows:

```
1
2
3
4
5
6
7
```

```
$ cd my-project/

# this blocks your terminal with the server logs; press Ctrl+C to stop it
$ symfony server:start

# this starts the server in the background so you can keep using the terminal
$ symfony serve -d
```

Browse your application by visiting the URL displayed by Symfony Server
(for example, `http://localhost:8000/`). You can also open the application
automatically:

```
1
2
3
4
5
```

```
# opens the application URL in your default browser
$ symfony open:local

# starts the server and opens the application in a single command
$ symfony server:start --open
```

Tip

Learn more about all available commands in the
[Symfony CLI documentation](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup/symfony_cli.html#symfony-cli-server).

Tip

The web server works with any PHP application, not only Symfony projects,
so it's a very useful generic development tool.

If you'd like to use Docker with Symfony, see [Using Docker with Symfony](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup/docker.html).

## [Installing Packages](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html\#installing-packages "Permalink to this headline")

A common practice when developing Symfony applications is to install packages
(Symfony calls them [bundles](https://symfony.com/doc/current/bundles.html)) that provide ready-to-use
features. Packages usually require some setup before using them (editing some
file to enable the bundle, creating some file to add some initial config, etc.)

Most of the time this setup can be automated and that's why Symfony includes
[Symfony Flex](https://github.com/symfony/flex), a tool to simplify the installation/removal of packages in
Symfony applications. Technically speaking, Symfony Flex is a Composer plugin
that is installed by default when creating a new Symfony application and which
**automates the most common tasks of Symfony applications**.

Tip

You can also [add Symfony Flex to an existing project](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup/flex.html).

Symfony Flex modifies the behavior of the `require`, `update`, and
`remove` Composer commands to provide advanced features. Consider the
following example:

```
1
2
```

```
$ cd my-project/
$ composer require logger
```

If you run that command in a Symfony application which doesn't use Flex, you'll
see a Composer error explaining that `logger` is not a valid package name.
However, if the application has Symfony Flex installed, that command installs
and enables all the packages needed to use the official Symfony logger.

This is possible because lots of Symfony packages/bundles define **"recipes"**,
which are a set of automated instructions to install and enable packages into
Symfony applications. Flex keeps track of the recipes it installed in a
`symfony.lock` file, which must be committed to your code repository.

Symfony Flex recipes are contributed by the community and they are stored in
two public repositories:

- [Main recipe repository](https://github.com/symfony/recipes) is a curated list of recipes for high quality and
maintained packages. Symfony Flex only looks in this repository by default.
- [Contrib recipe repository](https://github.com/symfony/recipes-contrib) contains all the recipes created by the
community. All of them are guaranteed to work, but their associated packages
could be unmaintained. Symfony Flex will ask your permission before installing
any of these recipes.

Read the [Symfony Recipes documentation](https://github.com/symfony/recipes/blob/master/README.rst) to learn everything about how to
create recipes for your own packages.

### [Symfony Packs](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html\#symfony-packs "Permalink to this headline")

Sometimes a single feature requires installing several packages and bundles.
Instead of installing them individually, Symfony provides **packs**, which are
Composer metapackages that include several dependencies.

For example, to add debugging features in your application, you can run the
`composer require --dev debug` command. This installs the `symfony/debug-pack`,
which in turn installs several packages like `symfony/debug-bundle`,
`symfony/monolog-bundle`, `symfony/var-dumper`, etc.

You won't see the `symfony/debug-pack` dependency in your `composer.json`,
as Flex automatically unpacks the pack. This means that it only adds the real
packages as dependencies (e.g. you will see a new `symfony/var-dumper` in
`require-dev`).

## [Checking Security Vulnerabilities](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html\#checking-security-vulnerabilities "Permalink to this headline")

The `symfony` binary created when you installed the [Symfony CLI](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html#setup-symfony-cli)
provides a command to check whether your project's dependencies contain any known security
vulnerability:

```
1
```

```
$ symfony check:security
```

A good security practice is to execute this command regularly to be able to
update or replace compromised dependencies as soon as possible. The security
check is done locally by fetching the public [PHP security advisories database](https://github.com/FriendsOfPHP/security-advisories),
so your `composer.lock` file is not sent on the network.

The `check:security` command terminates with a non-zero exit code if any of
your dependencies is affected by a known security vulnerability. This way you
can add it to your project build process and your continuous integration
workflows to make them fail when there are vulnerabilities.

Tip

In continuous integration services, run the `composer audit` command
instead. It doesn't require installing the Symfony CLI and it reports more
vulnerabilities, because Packagist combines the [PHP security advisories database](https://github.com/FriendsOfPHP/security-advisories)
used by `check:security` with the [GitHub Advisory Database](https://github.com/advisories).

## [Symfony LTS Versions](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html\#symfony-lts-versions "Permalink to this headline")

According to the [Symfony release process](https://symfony.com/doc/current/contributing/code/releases.html),
"long-term support" (or LTS for short) versions are published every two years.
Check out the [Symfony releases](https://symfony.com/releases) to know which is the latest LTS version.

By default, the command that creates new Symfony applications uses the latest
stable version. If you want to use an LTS version, add the `--version` option:

```
1
2
3
4
5
6
7
8
```

```
# use the most recent LTS version
$ symfony new my_project_directory --version=lts

# use the 'next' Symfony version to be released (still in development)
$ symfony new my_project_directory --version=next

# you can also select an exact specific Symfony version
$ symfony new my_project_directory --version="7.4.*"
```

The `lts` and `next` shortcuts are only available when using Symfony to
create new projects. If you use Composer, you need to tell the exact version:

```
1
```

```
$ composer create-project symfony/skeleton:"7.4.*" my_project_directory
```

## [The Symfony Demo application](https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html\#the-symfony-demo-application "Permalink to this headline")

[The Symfony Demo Application](https://github.com/symfony/demo) is a fully-functional application that shows the
recommended way to develop Symfony applications. It's a great learning tool for
Symfony newcomers and its code contains tons of comments and helpful notes.

Run this command to create a new project based on the Symfony Demo application:

```
1
```

```
$ symfony new my_project_directory --demo
```

<span id="symfony-tech-requirements"></span>
<div class="section">
<h2 id="technical-requirements"><a class="headerlink" href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html#technical-requirements" title="Permalink to this headline">Technical Requirements</a></h2>
<p>Before creating your first Symfony application you must:</p>
<ul>
    <li>Install PHP 8.4 or higher and these PHP extensions (which are installed and
enabled by default in most PHP 8 installations): <a href="https://www.php.net/book.ctype" class="reference external" rel="external noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Ctype</a>, <a href="https://www.php.net/book.iconv" class="reference external" rel="external noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">iconv</a>,
<a href="https://www.php.net/book.pcre" class="reference external" rel="external noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">PCRE</a>, <a href="https://www.php.net/book.session" class="reference external" rel="external noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Session</a>, <a href="https://www.php.net/book.simplexml" class="reference external" rel="external noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">SimpleXML</a>, and <a href="https://www.php.net/book.tokenizer" class="reference external" rel="external noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Tokenizer</a>;</li>
<li><a href="https://getcomposer.org/download/" class="reference external" rel="external noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Install Composer</a>, which is used to install PHP packages.</li>
</ul>
<span id="setup-symfony-cli"></span>
<p>Also, <a href="https://symfony.com/download" class="reference external">install the Symfony CLI</a>. This is optional, but it gives you a
helpful binary called <code translate="no" class="notranslate">symfony</code> that provides all tools you need to
develop and run your Symfony application locally.</p>
<p>The <code translate="no" class="notranslate">symfony</code> binary also provides a tool to check if your computer meets all
requirements. Open your console terminal and run this command:</p>
<div translate="no" data-loc="1" class="notranslate codeblock codeblock-length-sm codeblock-terminal codeblock-bash">
        <div class="codeblock-scroll">
        <pre class="codeblock-lines">1</pre>
        <pre class="codeblock-code"><code><span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>symfony check:requirements</code></pre>
    </div>
</div>
<div class="admonition admonition-note ">
    <p class="admonition-title">
                    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" fill="none" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" d="M11 5H6a2 2 0 00-2 2v11a2 2 0 002 2h11a2 2 0 002-2v-5m-1.414-9.414a2 2 0 112.828 2.828L11.828 15H9v-2.828l8.586-8.586z"></path></svg>
                <span>Note</span>
    </p><p>The Symfony CLI is open source, and you can contribute to it in the
<a href="https://github.com/symfony-cli/symfony-cli" class="reference external" rel="external noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">symfony-cli/symfony-cli GitHub repository</a>.</p>
</div>
<span id="creating-symfony-applications"></span>
</div>
<div class="section">
<h2 id="creating-symfony-applications"><a class="headerlink" href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html#creating-symfony-applications" title="Permalink to this headline">Creating Symfony Applications</a></h2>
<p>Open your console terminal and run any of these commands to create a new Symfony
application:</p>
<div translate="no" data-loc="5" class="notranslate codeblock codeblock-length-sm codeblock-terminal codeblock-bash">
        <div class="codeblock-scroll">
        <pre class="codeblock-lines">1
2
3
4
5</pre>
        <pre class="codeblock-code"><code><span class="hljs-comment"># run this if you are building a traditional web application</span>
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>symfony new my_project_directory --version=<span class="hljs-string">"8.1.*"</span> --webapp

<span class="hljs-comment"># run this if you are building a microservice, console application or API</span>
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>symfony new my_project_directory --version=<span class="hljs-string">"8.1.*"</span></code></pre>
    </div>
</div>
<p>The only difference between these two commands is the number of packages
installed by default. The <code translate="no" class="notranslate">--webapp</code> option installs extra packages to give
you everything you need to build a web application.</p>
<p>If you're not using the Symfony binary, run these commands to create the new
Symfony application using Composer:</p>
<div translate="no" data-loc="7" class="notranslate codeblock codeblock-length-sm codeblock-terminal codeblock-bash">
        <div class="codeblock-scroll">
        <pre class="codeblock-lines">1
2
3
4
5
6
7</pre>
        <pre class="codeblock-code"><code><span class="hljs-comment"># run this if you are building a traditional web application</span>
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>composer create-project symfony/skeleton:<span class="hljs-string">"8.1.*"</span> my_project_directory
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span><span class="hljs-built_in">cd</span> my_project_directory
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>composer require webapp

<span class="hljs-comment"># run this if you are building a microservice, console application or API</span>
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>composer create-project symfony/skeleton:<span class="hljs-string">"8.1.*"</span> my_project_directory</code></pre>
    </div>
</div>
<p>No matter which command you run to create the Symfony application, all of them
will create a new <code translate="no" class="notranslate">my_project_directory/</code> directory, download some dependencies
into it and even generate the basic directories and files you'll need to get
started. In other words, your new application is ready!</p>
<div class="admonition admonition-note ">
    <p class="admonition-title">
                    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" fill="none" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" d="M11 5H6a2 2 0 00-2 2v11a2 2 0 002 2h11a2 2 0 002-2v-5m-1.414-9.414a2 2 0 112.828 2.828L11.828 15H9v-2.828l8.586-8.586z"></path></svg>
                <span>Note</span>
    </p><p>The project's cache and logs directory (by default, <code translate="no" class="notranslate"><project>/var/cache/</code>
and <code translate="no" class="notranslate"><project>/var/log/</code>) must be writable by the web server. If you have
any issue, read how to <a href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup/file_permissions.html" class="reference internal">set up permissions for Symfony applications</a>.</p>
</div>
<span id="install-existing-app"></span>
</div>
<div class="section">
<h2 id="setting-up-an-existing-symfony-project"><a class="headerlink" href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html#setting-up-an-existing-symfony-project" title="Permalink to this headline">Setting up an Existing Symfony Project</a></h2>
<p>In addition to creating new Symfony projects, you will also work on projects
already created by other developers. In that case, you only need to get the
project code and install the dependencies with Composer. Assuming your team uses
Git, set up your project with the following commands:</p>
<div translate="no" data-loc="7" class="notranslate codeblock codeblock-length-sm codeblock-terminal codeblock-bash">
        <div class="codeblock-scroll">
        <pre class="codeblock-lines">1
2
3
4
5
6
7</pre>
        <pre class="codeblock-code"><code><span class="hljs-comment"># clone the project to download its contents</span>
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span><span class="hljs-built_in">cd</span> projects/
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>git <span class="hljs-built_in">clone</span> ...

<span class="hljs-comment"># make Composer install the project's dependencies into vendor/</span>
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span><span class="hljs-built_in">cd</span> my-project/
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>composer install</code></pre>
    </div>
</div>
<p>You'll probably also need to customize your <a href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/configuration.html#config-dot-env" class="reference internal">.env file</a>
and do a few other project-specific tasks (e.g. creating a database). When
working on an existing Symfony application for the first time, it may be useful
to run this command which displays information about the project:</p>
<div translate="no" data-loc="1" class="notranslate codeblock codeblock-length-sm codeblock-terminal codeblock-bash">
        <div class="codeblock-scroll">
        <pre class="codeblock-lines">1</pre>
        <pre class="codeblock-code"><code><span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>php bin/console about</code></pre>
    </div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="section">
<h2 id="running-symfony-applications"><a class="headerlink" href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html#running-symfony-applications" title="Permalink to this headline">Running Symfony Applications</a></h2>
<p>In production, you should install a web server like Nginx or Apache and
<a href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup/web_server_configuration.html" class="reference internal">configure it to run Symfony</a>. This
method can also be used if you're not using the Symfony local web server for
development.</p>
<span id="symfony-binary-web-server"></span>
<p>However for local development, the most convenient way of running Symfony is by
using the <a href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup/symfony_cli.html#symfony-cli-server" class="reference internal">local web server</a> provided by the
Symfony CLI tool. This local server provides support for HTTP/2, concurrent
requests, TLS/SSL and automatic generation of security certificates, among
other things.</p>
<p>Open your terminal, move into your new project directory and start the local web
server as follows:</p>
<div translate="no" data-loc="7" class="notranslate codeblock codeblock-length-sm codeblock-terminal codeblock-bash">
        <div class="codeblock-scroll">
        <pre class="codeblock-lines">1
2
3
4
5
6
7</pre>
        <pre class="codeblock-code"><code><span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span><span class="hljs-built_in">cd</span> my-project/

<span class="hljs-comment"># this blocks your terminal with the server logs; press Ctrl+C to stop it</span>
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>symfony server:start

<span class="hljs-comment"># this starts the server in the background so you can keep using the terminal</span>
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>symfony serve -d</code></pre>
    </div>
</div>
<p>Browse your application by visiting the URL displayed by Symfony Server
(for example, <code translate="no" class="notranslate">http://localhost:8000/</code>). You can also open the application
automatically:</p>
<div translate="no" data-loc="5" class="notranslate codeblock codeblock-length-sm codeblock-terminal codeblock-bash">
        <div class="codeblock-scroll">
        <pre class="codeblock-lines">1
2
3
4
5</pre>
        <pre class="codeblock-code"><code><span class="hljs-comment"># opens the application URL in your default browser</span>
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>symfony open:<span class="hljs-built_in">local</span>

<span class="hljs-comment"># starts the server and opens the application in a single command</span>
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>symfony server:start --open</code></pre>
    </div>
</div>
<div class="admonition admonition-tip ">
    <p class="admonition-title">
                    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" fill="none" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" d="M9.663 17h4.673M12 3v1m6.364 1.636l-.707.707M21 12h-1M4 12H3m3.343-5.657l-.707-.707m2.828 9.9a5 5 0 117.072 0l-.548.547A3.374 3.374 0 0014 18.469V19a2 2 0 11-4 0v-.531c0-.895-.356-1.754-.988-2.386l-.548-.547z"></path></svg>
                <span>Tip</span>
    </p><p>Learn more about all available commands in the
<a href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup/symfony_cli.html#symfony-cli-server" class="reference internal">Symfony CLI documentation</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonition admonition-tip ">
    <p class="admonition-title">
                    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" fill="none" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" d="M9.663 17h4.673M12 3v1m6.364 1.636l-.707.707M21 12h-1M4 12H3m3.343-5.657l-.707-.707m2.828 9.9a5 5 0 117.072 0l-.548.547A3.374 3.374 0 0014 18.469V19a2 2 0 11-4 0v-.531c0-.895-.356-1.754-.988-2.386l-.548-.547z"></path></svg>
                <span>Tip</span>
    </p><p>The web server works with any PHP application, not only Symfony projects,
so it's a very useful generic development tool.</p>
</div>
<div class="section">
<h3 id="symfony-docker-integration"><a class="headerlink" href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html#symfony-docker-integration" title="Permalink to this headline">Symfony Docker Integration</a></h3>
<p>If you'd like to use Docker with Symfony, see <a href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup/docker.html" class="reference internal">Using Docker with Symfony</a>.</p>
<span id="symfony-flex"></span>
<span id="flex-quick-intro"></span>
</div>
</div>
<div class="section">
<h2 id="installing-packages"><a class="headerlink" href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html#installing-packages" title="Permalink to this headline">Installing Packages</a></h2>
<p>A common practice when developing Symfony applications is to install packages
(Symfony calls them <a href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/bundles.html" class="reference internal">bundles</a>) that provide ready-to-use
features. Packages usually require some setup before using them (editing some
file to enable the bundle, creating some file to add some initial config, etc.)</p>
<p>Most of the time this setup can be automated and that's why Symfony includes
<a href="https://github.com/symfony/flex" class="reference external" rel="external noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Symfony Flex</a>, a tool to simplify the installation/removal of packages in
Symfony applications. Technically speaking, Symfony Flex is a Composer plugin
that is installed by default when creating a new Symfony application and which
<strong>automates the most common tasks of Symfony applications</strong>.</p>
<div class="admonition admonition-tip ">
    <p class="admonition-title">
                    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" fill="none" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" d="M9.663 17h4.673M12 3v1m6.364 1.636l-.707.707M21 12h-1M4 12H3m3.343-5.657l-.707-.707m2.828 9.9a5 5 0 117.072 0l-.548.547A3.374 3.374 0 0014 18.469V19a2 2 0 11-4 0v-.531c0-.895-.356-1.754-.988-2.386l-.548-.547z"></path></svg>
                <span>Tip</span>
    </p><p>You can also <a href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup/flex.html" class="reference internal">add Symfony Flex to an existing project</a>.</p>
</div>
<p>Symfony Flex modifies the behavior of the <code translate="no" class="notranslate">require</code>, <code translate="no" class="notranslate">update</code>, and
<code translate="no" class="notranslate">remove</code> Composer commands to provide advanced features. Consider the
following example:</p>
<div translate="no" data-loc="2" class="notranslate codeblock codeblock-length-sm codeblock-terminal codeblock-bash">
        <div class="codeblock-scroll">
        <pre class="codeblock-lines">1
2</pre>
        <pre class="codeblock-code"><code><span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span><span class="hljs-built_in">cd</span> my-project/
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>composer require logger</code></pre>
    </div>
</div>
<p>If you run that command in a Symfony application which doesn't use Flex, you'll
see a Composer error explaining that <code translate="no" class="notranslate">logger</code> is not a valid package name.
However, if the application has Symfony Flex installed, that command installs
and enables all the packages needed to use the official Symfony logger.</p>
<span id="recipes-description"></span>
<p>This is possible because lots of Symfony packages/bundles define <strong>"recipes"</strong>,
which are a set of automated instructions to install and enable packages into
Symfony applications. Flex keeps track of the recipes it installed in a
<code translate="no" class="notranslate">symfony.lock</code> file, which must be committed to your code repository.</p>
<p>Symfony Flex recipes are contributed by the community and they are stored in
two public repositories:</p>
<ul>
    <li><a href="https://github.com/symfony/recipes" class="reference external" rel="external noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Main recipe repository</a> is a curated list of recipes for high quality and
maintained packages. Symfony Flex only looks in this repository by default.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/symfony/recipes-contrib" class="reference external" rel="external noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Contrib recipe repository</a> contains all the recipes created by the
community. All of them are guaranteed to work, but their associated packages
could be unmaintained. Symfony Flex will ask your permission before installing
any of these recipes.</li>
</ul>
<p>Read the <a href="https://github.com/symfony/recipes/blob/master/README.rst" class="reference external" rel="external noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Symfony Recipes documentation</a> to learn everything about how to
create recipes for your own packages.</p>
<span id="symfony-packs"></span>
<div class="section">
<h3 id="symfony-packs"><a class="headerlink" href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html#symfony-packs" title="Permalink to this headline">Symfony Packs</a></h3>
<p>Sometimes a single feature requires installing several packages and bundles.
Instead of installing them individually, Symfony provides <strong>packs</strong>, which are
Composer metapackages that include several dependencies.</p>
<p>For example, to add debugging features in your application, you can run the
<code translate="no" class="notranslate">composer require --dev debug</code> command. This installs the <code translate="no" class="notranslate">symfony/debug-pack</code>,
which in turn installs several packages like <code translate="no" class="notranslate">symfony/debug-bundle</code>,
<code translate="no" class="notranslate">symfony/monolog-bundle</code>, <code translate="no" class="notranslate">symfony/var-dumper</code>, etc.</p>
<p>You won't see the <code translate="no" class="notranslate">symfony/debug-pack</code> dependency in your <code translate="no" class="notranslate">composer.json</code>,
as Flex automatically unpacks the pack. This means that it only adds the real
packages as dependencies (e.g. you will see a new <code translate="no" class="notranslate">symfony/var-dumper</code> in
<code translate="no" class="notranslate">require-dev</code>).</p>
<span id="security-checker"></span>
</div>
</div>
<div class="section">
<h2 id="checking-security-vulnerabilities"><a class="headerlink" href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html#checking-security-vulnerabilities" title="Permalink to this headline">Checking Security Vulnerabilities</a></h2>
<p>The <code translate="no" class="notranslate">symfony</code> binary created when you installed the <a href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html#setup-symfony-cli" class="reference internal">Symfony CLI</a>
provides a command to check whether your project's dependencies contain any known security
vulnerability:</p>
<div translate="no" data-loc="1" class="notranslate codeblock codeblock-length-sm codeblock-terminal codeblock-bash">
        <div class="codeblock-scroll">
        <pre class="codeblock-lines">1</pre>
        <pre class="codeblock-code"><code><span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>symfony check:security</code></pre>
    </div>
</div>
<p>A good security practice is to execute this command regularly to be able to
update or replace compromised dependencies as soon as possible. The security
check is done locally by fetching the public <a href="https://github.com/FriendsOfPHP/security-advisories" class="reference external" rel="external noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">PHP security advisories database</a>,
so your <code translate="no" class="notranslate">composer.lock</code> file is not sent on the network.</p>
<p>The <code translate="no" class="notranslate">check:security</code> command terminates with a non-zero exit code if any of
your dependencies is affected by a known security vulnerability. This way you
can add it to your project build process and your continuous integration
workflows to make them fail when there are vulnerabilities.</p>
<div class="admonition admonition-tip ">

used by <code translate="no" class="notranslate">check:security</code> with the <a href="https://github.com/advisories" class="reference external" rel="external noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">GitHub Advisory Database</a>.</p>

<h2 id="symfony-lts-versions"><a class="headerlink" href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/setup.html#symfony-lts-versions" title="Permalink to this headline">Symfony LTS Versions</a></h2>
<p>According to the <a href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/contributing/code/releases.html" class="reference internal">Symfony release process</a>,
"long-term support" (or LTS for short) versions are published every two years.
Check out the <a href="https://symfony.com/releases" class="reference external">Symfony releases</a> to know which is the latest LTS version.</p>
<p>By default, the command that creates new Symfony applications uses the latest
stable version. If you want to use an LTS version, add the <code translate="no" class="notranslate">--version</code> option:</p>
<div translate="no" data-loc="8" class="notranslate codeblock codeblock-length-sm codeblock-terminal codeblock-bash">
        <div class="codeblock-scroll">
        <pre class="codeblock-lines">1
2
3
4
5
6
7
8</pre>
        <pre class="codeblock-code"><code><span class="hljs-comment"># use the most recent LTS version</span>
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>symfony new my_project_directory --version=lts

<span class="hljs-comment"># use the 'next' Symfony version to be released (still in development)</span>
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>symfony new my_project_directory --version=next

<span class="hljs-comment"># you can also select an exact specific Symfony version</span>
<span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>symfony new my_project_directory --version=<span class="hljs-string">"7.4.*"</span></code></pre>
    </div>
</div>
<p>The <code translate="no" class="notranslate">lts</code> and <code translate="no" class="notranslate">next</code> shortcuts are only available when using Symfony to
create new projects. If you use Composer, you need to tell the exact version:</p>
<div translate="no" data-loc="1" class="notranslate codeblock codeblock-length-sm codeblock-terminal codeblock-bash">
        <div class="codeblock-scroll">
        <pre class="codeblock-lines">1</pre>
        <pre class="codeblock-code"><code><span class="hljs-prompt">$ </span>composer create-project symfony/skeleton:<span class="hljs-string">"7.4.*"</span> my_project_directory</code></pre>
    </div>

The `--webapp` option installs extra packages to give\\nyou everything you need to build a web application.\\n\\nIf you\u0027re not using the Symfony binary, run these commands to create the new\\nSymfony application using Composer:\\n\\n```\\n1\\n2\\n3\\n4\\n5\\n6\\n7\\n```\\n\\n```\\n# run this if you are building a traditional web application\\n$ composer create-project symfony\\\/skeleton:\\\u00228.1.*\\\u0022 my_project_directory\\n$ cd my_project_directory\\n$ composer require webapp\\n\\n# run this if you are building a microservice, console application or API\\n$ composer create-project symfony\\\/skeleton:\\\u00228.1.*\\\u0022 my_project_directory\\n```\\n\\nNo matter which command you run to create the Symfony application, all of them\\nwill create a new `my_project_directory\\\/` directory, download some dependencies\\ninto it and even generate the basic directories and files you\u0027ll need to get\\nstarted. In other words, your new application is ready!\\n\\nNote\\n\\nThe project\u0027s cache and logs directory (by default, `\u003Cproject\u003E\\\/var\\\/cache\\\/`\\nand `\u003Cproject\u003E\\\/var\\\/log\\\/`) must be writable by the web server. If you have\\nany issue, read how to [set up permissions for Symfony applications](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup\\\/file_permissions.html).\\n\\n## [Setting up an Existing Symfony Project](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup.html\\\\#setting-up-an-existing-symfony-project \\\u0022Permalink to this headline\\\u0022)\\n\\nIn addition to creating new Symfony projects, you will also work on projects\\nalready created by other developers. In that case, you only need to get the\\nproject code and install the dependencies with Composer. Assuming your team uses\\nGit, set up your project with the following commands:\\n\\n```\\n1\\n2\\n3\\n4\\n5\\n6\\n7\\n```\\n\\n```\\n# clone the project to download its contents\\n$ cd projects\\\/\\n$ git clone ...\\n\\n# make Composer install the project\u0027s dependencies into vendor\\\/\\n$ cd my-project\\\/\\n$ composer install\\n```\\n\\nYou\u0027ll probably also need to customize your [.env file](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/configuration.html#config-dot-env)\\nand do a few other project-specific tasks (e.g. creating a database). When\\nworking on an existing Symfony application for the first time, it may be useful\\nto run this command which displays information about the project:\\n\\n```\\n1\\n```\\n\\n```\\n$ php bin\\\/console about\\n```\\n\\n## [Running Symfony Applications](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup.html\\\\#running-symfony-applications \\\u0022Permalink to this headline\\\u0022)\\n\\nIn production, you should install a web server like Nginx or Apache and\\n[configure it to run Symfony](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup\\\/web_server_configuration.html). This\\nmethod can also be used if you\u0027re not using the Symfony local web server for\\ndevelopment.\\n\\nHowever for local development, the most convenient way of running Symfony is by\\nusing the [local web server](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup\\\/symfony_cli.html#symfony-cli-server) provided by the\\nSymfony CLI tool. This local server provides support for HTTP\\\/2, concurrent\\nrequests, TLS\\\/SSL and automatic generation of security certificates, among\\nother things.\\n\\nOpen your terminal, move into your new project directory and start the local web\\nserver as follows:\\n\\n```\\n1\\n2\\n3\\n4\\n5\\n6\\n7\\n```\\n\\n```\\n$ cd my-project\\\/\\n\\n# this blocks your terminal with the server logs; press Ctrl+C to stop it\\n$ symfony server:start\\n\\n# this starts the server in the background so you can keep using the terminal\\n$ symfony serve -d\\n```\\n\\nBrowse your application by visiting the URL displayed by Symfony Server\\n(for example, `http:\\\/\\\/localhost:8000\\\/`). You can also open the application\\nautomatically:\\n\\n```\\n1\\n2\\n3\\n4\\n5\\n```\\n\\n```\\n# opens the application URL in your default browser\\n$ symfony open:local\\n\\n# starts the server and opens the application in a single command\\n$ symfony server:start --open\\n```\\n\\nTip\\n\\nLearn more about all available commands in the\\n[Symfony CLI documentation](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup\\\/symfony_cli.html#symfony-cli-server).\\n\\nTip\\n\\nThe web server works with any PHP application, not only Symfony projects,\\nso it\u0027s a very useful generic development tool.\\n\\n### [Symfony Docker Integration](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup.html\\\\#symfony-docker-integration \\\u0022Permalink to this headline\\\u0022)\\n\\nIf you\u0027d like to use Docker with Symfony, see [Using Docker with Symfony](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup\\\/docker.html).\\n\\n## [Installing Packages](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup.html\\\\#installing-packages \\\u0022Permalink to this headline\\\u0022)\\n\\nA common practice when developing Symfony applications is to install packages\\n(Symfony calls them [bundles](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/bundles.html)) that provide ready-to-use\\nfeatures. Packages usually require some setup before using them (editing some\\nfile to enable the bundle, creating some file to add some initial config, etc.)\\n\\nMost of the time this setup can be automated and that\u0027s why Symfony includes\\n[Symfony Flex](https:\\\/\\\/github.com\\\/symfony\\\/flex), a tool to simplify the installation\\\/removal of packages in\\nSymfony applications. Technically speaking, Symfony Flex is a Composer plugin\\nthat is installed by default when creating a new Symfony application and which\\n**automates the most common tasks of Symfony applications**.\\n\\nTip\\n\\nYou can also [add Symfony Flex to an existing project](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup\\\/flex.html).\\n\\nSymfony Flex modifies the behavior of the `require`, `update`, and\\n`remove` Composer commands to provide advanced features. Consider the\\nfollowing example:\\n\\n```\\n1\\n2\\n```\\n\\n```\\n$ cd my-project\\\/\\n$ composer require logger\\n```\\n\\nIf you run that command in a Symfony application which doesn\u0027t use Flex, you\u0027ll\\nsee a Composer error explaining that `logger` is not a valid package name.\\nHowever, if the application has Symfony Flex installed, that command installs\\nand enables all the packages needed to use the official Symfony logger.\\n\\nThis is possible because lots of Symfony packages\\\/bundles define **\\\u0022recipes\\\u0022**,\\nwhich are a set of automated instructions to install and enable packages into\\nSymfony applications. Flex keeps track of the recipes it installed in a\\n`symfony.lock` file, which must be committed to your code repository.\\n\\nSymfony Flex recipes are contributed by the community and they are stored in\\ntwo public repositories:\\n\\n- [Main recipe repository](https:\\\/\\\/github.com\\\/symfony\\\/recipes) is a curated list of recipes for high quality and\\nmaintained packages. Symfony Flex only looks in this repository by default.\\n- [Contrib recipe repository](https:\\\/\\\/github.com\\\/symfony\\\/recipes-contrib) contains all the recipes created by the\\ncommunity. All of them are guaranteed to work, but their associated packages\\ncould be unmaintained. Symfony Flex will ask your permission before installing\\nany of these recipes.\\n\\nRead the [Symfony Recipes documentation](https:\\\/\\\/github.com\\\/symfony\\\/recipes\\\/blob\\\/master\\\/README.rst) to learn everything about how to\\ncreate recipes for your own packages.\\n\\n### [Symfony Packs](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup.html\\\\#symfony-packs \\\u0022Permalink to this headline\\\u0022)\\n\\nSometimes a single feature requires installing several packages and bundles.\\nInstead of installing them individually, Symfony provides **packs**, which are\\nComposer metapackages that include several dependencies.\\n\\nFor example, to add debugging features in your application, you can run the\\n`composer require --dev debug` command. This installs the `symfony\\\/debug-pack`,\\nwhich in turn installs several packages like `symfony\\\/debug-bundle`,\\n`symfony\\\/monolog-bundle`, `symfony\\\/var-dumper`, etc.\\n\\nYou won\u0027t see the `symfony\\\/debug-pack` dependency in your `composer.json`,\\nas Flex automatically unpacks the pack. This means that it only adds the real\\npackages as dependencies (e.g. you will see a new `symfony\\\/var-dumper` in\\n`require-dev`).\\n\\n## [Checking Security Vulnerabilities](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup.html\\\\#checking-security-vulnerabilities \\\u0022Permalink to this headline\\\u0022)\\n\\nThe `symfony` binary created when you installed the [Symfony CLI](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup.html#setup-symfony-cli)\\nprovides a command to check whether your project\u0027s dependencies contain any known security\\nvulnerability:\\n\\n```\\n1\\n```\\n\\n```\\n$ symfony check:security\\n```\\n\\nA good security practice is to execute this command regularly to be able to\\nupdate or replace compromised dependencies as soon as possible. The security\\ncheck is done locally by fetching the public [PHP security advisories database](https:\\\/\\\/github.com\\\/FriendsOfPHP\\\/security-advisories),\\nso your `composer.lock` file is not sent on the network.\\n\\nThe `check:security` command terminates with a non-zero exit code if any of\\nyour dependencies is affected by a known security vulnerability. This way you\\ncan add it to your project build process and your continuous integration\\nworkflows to make them fail when there are vulnerabilities.\\n\\nTip\\n\\nIn continuous integration services, run the `composer audit` command\\ninstead. It doesn\u0027t require installing the Symfony CLI and it reports more\\nvulnerabilities, because Packagist combines the [PHP security advisories database](https:\\\/\\\/github.com\\\/FriendsOfPHP\\\/security-advisories)\\nused by `check:security` with the [GitHub Advisory Database](https:\\\/\\\/github.com\\\/advisories).\\n\\n## [Symfony LTS Versions](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup.html\\\\#symfony-lts-versions \\\u0022Permalink to this headline\\\u0022)\\n\\nAccording to the [Symfony release process](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/contributing\\\/code\\\/releases.html),\\n\\\u0022long-term support\\\u0022 (or LTS for short) versions are published every two years.\\nCheck out the [Symfony releases](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/releases) to know which is the latest LTS version.\\n\\nBy default, the command that creates new Symfony applications uses the latest\\nstable version. If you want to use an LTS version, add the `--version` option:\\n\\n```\\n1\\n2\\n3\\n4\\n5\\n6\\n7\\n8\\n```\\n\\n```\\n# use the most recent LTS version\\n$ symfony new my_project_directory --version=lts\\n\\n# use the \u0027next\u0027 Symfony version to be released (still in development)\\n$ symfony new my_project_directory --version=next\\n\\n# you can also select an exact specific Symfony version\\n$ symfony new my_project_directory --version=\\\u00227.4.*\\\u0022\\n```\\n\\nThe `lts` and `next` shortcuts are only available when using Symfony to\\ncreate new projects. If you use Composer, you need to tell the exact version:\\n\\n```\\n1\\n```\\n\\n```\\n$ composer create-project symfony\\\/skeleton:\\\u00227.4.*\\\u0022 my_project_directory\\n```\\n\\n## [The Symfony Demo application](https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup.html\\\\#the-symfony-demo-application \\\u0022Permalink to this headline\\\u0022)\\n\\n[The Symfony Demo Application](https:\\\/\\\/github.com\\\/symfony\\\/demo) is a fully-functional application that shows the\\nrecommended way to develop Symfony applications. title=\\\u0022Permalink to this headline\\\u0022\u003EInstalling Packages\u003C\\\/a\u003E\u003C\\\/h2\u003E\\n\u003Cp\u003EA common practice when developing Symfony applications is to install Packages usually require some setup before using them (editing some\\nfile to enable the bundle, creating some file to add some initial config, etc.)\u003C\\\/p\u003E\\n\u003Cp\u003EMost of the time this setup can be automated and that\u0027s why Symfony includes\\n\u003Ca href=\\\u0022https:\\\/\\\/github.com\\\/symfony\\\/flex\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022reference external\\\u0022 rel=\\\u0022external noopener noreferrer\\\u0022 target=\\\u0022_blank\\\u0022\u003ESymfony Flex\u003C\\\/a\u003E, a tool to simplify the installation\\\/removal of packages in\\nSymfony applications. Technically speaking, Symfony Flex is a Composer plugin\\nthat is installed by default when creating a new Symfony application and which\\n\u003Cstrong\u003Eautomates the most common tasks of Symfony applications\u003C\\\/strong\u003E.\u003C\\\/p\u003E\\n\u003Cdiv class=\\\u0022admonition admonition-tip \\\u0022\u003E\\n    \u003Cp class=\\\u0022admonition-title\\\u0022\u003E\\n                    \u003Csvg xmlns=\\\u0022http:\\\/\\\/www.w3.org\\\/2000\\\/svg\\\u0022 fill=\\\u0022none\\\u0022 width=\\\u002224\\\u0022 height=\\\u002224\\\u0022 viewBox=\\\u00220 0 24 24\\\u0022 stroke=\\\u0022currentColor\\\u0022\u003E\u003Cpath stroke-linecap=\\\u0022round\\\u0022 stroke-linejoin=\\\u0022round\\\u0022 stroke-width=\\\u00222\\\u0022 d=\\\u0022M9.663 17h4.673M12 3v1m6.364 1.636l-.707.707M21 12h-1M4 12H3m3.343-5.657l-.707-.707m2.828 9.9a5 5 0 117.072 0l-.548.547A3.374 3.374 0 0014 18.469V19a2 2 0 11-4 0v-.531c0-.895-.356-1.754-.988-2.386l-.548-.547z\\\u0022\u003E\u003C\\\/path\u003E\u003C\\\/svg\u003E\\n                \u003Cspan\u003ETip\u003C\\\/span\u003E\\n    \u003C\\\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EYou can also \u003Ca href=\\\u0022https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup\\\/flex.html\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022reference internal\\\u0022\u003Eadd Symfony Flex to an existing project\u003C\\\/a\u003E.\u003C\\\/p\u003E\\n\u003C\\\/div\u003E\\n\u003Cp\u003ESymfony Flex modifies the behavior of the \u003Ccode translate=\\\u0022no\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022notranslate\\\u0022\u003Erequire\u003C\\\/code\u003E, \u003Ccode translate=\\\u0022no\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022notranslate\\\u0022\u003Eupdate\u003C\\\/code\u003E, and\\n\u003Ccode translate=\\\u0022no\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022notranslate\\\u0022\u003Eremove\u003C\\\/code\u003E Composer commands to provide advanced features. Consider the\\nfollowing example:\u003C\\\/p\u003E\\n\u003Cdiv translate=\\\u0022no\\\u0022 data-loc=\\\u00222\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022notranslate codeblock codeblock-length-sm codeblock-terminal codeblock-bash\\\u0022\u003E\\n        \u003Cdiv class=\\\u0022codeblock-scroll\\\u0022\u003E\\n        \u003Cpre class=\\\u0022codeblock-lines\\\u0022\u003E1\\n2\u003C\\\/pre\u003E\\n        \u003Cpre class=\\\u0022codeblock-code\\\u0022\u003E\u003Ccode\u003E\u003Cspan class=\\\u0022hljs-prompt\\\u0022\u003E$ \u003C\\\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\\\u0022hljs-built_in\\\u0022\u003Ecd\u003C\\\/span\u003E my-project\\\/\\n\u003Cspan class=\\\u0022hljs-prompt\\\u0022\u003E$ \u003C\\\/span\u003Ecomposer require logger\u003C\\\/code\u003E\u003C\\\/pre\u003E\\n    \u003C\\\/div\u003E\\n\u003C\\\/div\u003E\\n\u003Cp\u003EIf you run that command in a Symfony application which doesn\u0027t use Flex, you\u0027ll\\nsee a Composer error explaining that \u003Ccode translate=\\\u0022no\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022notranslate\\\u0022\u003Elogger\u003C\\\/code\u003E is not a valid package name.\\nHowever, if the application has Symfony Flex installed, that command installs\\nand enables all the packages needed to use the official Symfony logger.\u003C\\\/p\u003E\\n\u003Cspan id=\\\u0022recipes-description\\\u0022\u003E\u003C\\\/span\u003E\\n\u003Cp\u003EThis is possible because lots of Symfony packages\\\/bundles define \u003Cstrong\u003E\\\u0022recipes\\\u0022\u003C\\\/strong\u003E,\\nwhich are a set of automated instructions to install and enable packages into\\nSymfony applications. Flex keeps track of the recipes it installed in a\\n\u003Ccode translate=\\\u0022no\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022notranslate\\\u0022\u003Esymfony.lock\u003C\\\/code\u003E file, which must be committed to your code repository.\u003C\\\/p\u003E\\n\u003Cp\u003ESymfony Flex recipes are contributed by the community and they are stored in\\ntwo public repositories:\u003C\\\/p\u003E\\n\u003Cul\u003E\\n    \u003Cli\u003E\u003Ca href=\\\u0022https:\\\/\\\/github.com\\\/symfony\\\/recipes\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022reference external\\\u0022 rel=\\\u0022external noopener noreferrer\\\u0022 target=\\\u0022_blank\\\u0022\u003EMain recipe repository\u003C\\\/a\u003E is a curated list of recipes for high quality and\\nmaintained packages. Symfony Flex only looks in this repository by default.\u003C\\\/li\u003E\\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Ca href=\\\u0022https:\\\/\\\/github.com\\\/symfony\\\/recipes-contrib\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022reference external\\\u0022 rel=\\\u0022external noopener noreferrer\\\u0022 target=\\\u0022_blank\\\u0022\u003EContrib recipe repository\u003C\\\/a\u003E contains all the recipes created by the\\ncommunity. All of them are guaranteed to work, but their associated packages\\ncould be unmaintained. Symfony Flex will ask your permission before installing\\nany of these recipes.\u003C\\\/li\u003E\\n\u003C\\\/ul\u003E\\n\u003Cp\u003ERead the \u003Ca href=\\\u0022https:\\\/\\\/github.com\\\/symfony\\\/recipes\\\/blob\\\/master\\\/README.rst\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022reference external\\\u0022 rel=\\\u0022external noopener noreferrer\\\u0022 target=\\\u0022_blank\\\u0022\u003ESymfony Recipes documentation\u003C\\\/a\u003E to learn everything about how to\\ncreate recipes for your own packages.\u003C\\\/p\u003E\\n\u003Cspan id=\\\u0022symfony-packs\\\u0022\u003E\u003C\\\/span\u003E\\n\u003Cdiv class=\\\u0022section\\\u0022\u003E\\n\u003Ch3 id=\\\u0022symfony-packs\\\u0022\u003E\u003Ca class=\\\u0022headerlink\\\u0022 href=\\\u0022https:\\\/\\\/symfony.com\\\/doc\\\/current\\\/setup.html#symfony-packs\\\u0022 title=\\\u0022Permalink to this headline\\\u0022\u003ESymfony Packs\u003C\\\/a\u003E\u003C\\\/h3\u003E\\n\u003Cp\u003ESometimes a single feature requires installing several packages and bundles.\\nInstead of installing them individually, Symfony provides \u003Cstrong\u003Epacks\u003C\\\/strong\u003E, which are\\nComposer metapackages that include several dependencies.\u003C\\\/p\u003E\\n\u003Cp\u003EFor example, to add debugging features in your application, you can run the\\n\u003Ccode translate=\\\u0022no\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022notranslate\\\u0022\u003Ecomposer require --dev debug\u003C\\\/code\u003E command. This installs the \u003Ccode translate=\\\u0022no\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022notranslate\\\u0022\u003Esymfony\\\/debug-pack\u003C\\\/code\u003E,\\nwhich in turn installs several packages like \u003Ccode translate=\\\u0022no\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022notranslate\\\u0022\u003Esymfony\\\/debug-bundle\u003C\\\/code\u003E,\\n\u003Ccode translate=\\\u0022no\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022notranslate\\\u0022\u003Esymfony\\\/monolog-bundle\u003C\\\/code\u003E, \u003Ccode translate=\\\u0022no\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022notranslate\\\u0022\u003Esymfony\\\/var-dumper\u003C\\\/code\u003E, etc.\u003C\\\/p\u003E\\n\u003Cp\u003EYou won\u0027t see the \u003Ccode translate=\\\u0022no\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022notranslate\\\u0022\u003Esymfony\\\/debug-pack\u003C\\\/code\u003E dependency in your \u003Ccode translate=\\\u0022no\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022notranslate\\\u0022\u003Ecomposer.json\u003C\\\/code\u003E,\\nas Flex automatically unpacks the pack. data-loc=\\\u00221\\\u0022 class=\\\u0022notranslate codeblock codeblock-length-sm codeblock-terminal codeblock-bash\\\u0022\u003E\\n        \u003Cdiv class=\\\u0022codeblock-scroll\\\u0022\u003E\\n class=\\\u0022hljs-prompt\\\u0022\u003E$ \u003C\\\/span\u003Esymfony check:security\u003C\\\/code\u003E\u003C\\\/pre\u003E\\n    \u003C\\\/div\u003E\\n\u003C\\\/div\u003E\\n\u003Cp\u003EA good
